title: 10 Neighborhoods, One Reason Each
description: Ten Durban localities, each anchored by one specific institution, landscape, or recurring event.

cards.title: Berea
cards.subtitle: For Africa’s oldest surviving botanic garden
cards.notes: Durban Botanic Gardens occupies 15 hectares on the Berea side of the city centre.
cards.short_summary: The neighborhood’s botanic garden conserves indigenous and exotic plant collections, including cycads, palms, bromeliads, and orchids.
cards.source_title: eThekwini Municipality — “Spring Has Sprung in the City’s Blossoming Gardens”

cards.title: Morningside
cards.subtitle: For a municipal park with a walk-through aviary
cards.notes: Mitchell Park combines picnic lawns and a children’s play area with its small zoo park.
cards.short_summary: The zoo park’s animal collection includes birds housed in a walk-through aviary.
cards.source_title: eThekwini Municipality — “Spring Has Sprung in the City’s Blossoming Gardens”

cards.title: Durban North
cards.subtitle: For the paths and ponds of the Japanese Gardens
cards.notes: The municipal garden’s walking paths circle ponds planted with water lilies.
cards.short_summary: Japanese-style ponds and a network of walking paths give this locality a distinct public garden.
cards.source_title: eThekwini Municipality — “Spring Has Sprung in the City’s Blossoming Gardens”

cards.title: North Beach
cards.subtitle: For a garden between the promenade and the hotels
cards.notes: Amphitheatre Gardens sits on the Golden Mile between the beachfront promenade and the hotel strip.
cards.short_summary: Its ponds, fountains, and subtropical planting form a small landscaped pause beside the beachfront.
cards.source_title: eThekwini Municipality — “Spring Has Sprung in the City’s Blossoming Gardens”

cards.title: Glenwood
cards.subtitle: For a nonprofit contemporary-art space
cards.notes: KZNSA Gallery operates from Bulwer Road as a nonprofit devoted to advancing visual art.
cards.short_summary: Its exhibition program gives Glenwood a standing address for contemporary visual art.

cards.title: Yellowwood Park
cards.subtitle: For a 210-hectare protected area inside the suburb
cards.notes: Kenneth Stainbank Nature Reserve is situated within Yellowwood Park, southwest of central Durban.
cards.short_summary: A substantial protected landscape is embedded directly in this residential locality.
cards.source_title: Ezemvelo KZN Wildlife — Kenneth Stainbank Nature Reserve Management Plan

cards.title: Inanda
cards.subtitle: For Gandhi’s Phoenix Settlement
cards.notes: The settlement was established in 1904 and later became home to the press that published Indian Opinion.
cards.short_summary: Phoenix Settlement preserves a documented site from Gandhi’s years in South Africa.
cards.source_title: Phoenix Settlement Trust — About Phoenix Settlement

cards.title: Greyville
cards.subtitle: For the annual Durban July
cards.notes: The Durban July is staged at Hollywoodbets Greyville Racecourse on Avondale Road.
cards.short_summary: Greyville’s namesake racecourse is the fixed venue for Durban’s annual July race meeting.

cards.title: Durban Central
cards.subtitle: For natural-science galleries inside City Hall
cards.notes: The first-floor museum presents public natural-science galleries and curriculum-linked programs.
cards.short_summary: Durban Natural Science Museum places a public science collection within the civic center.
cards.source_title: eThekwini Municipality — Parks, Recreation & Culture Amenities

cards.title: Westville
cards.subtitle: For a municipal local-history museum
cards.notes: Bergtheil Museum is one of eThekwini’s managed Local History Museum sites and stands on Queens Avenue.
cards.short_summary: Westville has its own branch in the municipality’s local-history museum network.
cards.source_title: eThekwini Municipality — Parks, Recreation & Culture Amenities
